quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry about it.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up.
Leave the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. If you can do so safely, change lanes and let them go by. Speeding up may only make them follow you faster.

questions.question: When riding at night, which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.
Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to avoid crashes. Use the headlights of cars ahead to see the road better. Use your high beam, but turn it off when you meet or follow another vehicle.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, the horn:

options.text: Is useless.
Usually cannot be heard by other drivers.
Can get someone's attention quickly.
Should never be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can get someone's attention quickly.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help you get someone's attention quickly. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn, so other drivers may not hear it. Do not rely only on your horn to handle a hazard.

questions.question: What protection do goggles provide?

options.text: Protection for your eyes and face.
Protection for your face but not your eyes.
Protection for your eyes but not your face.
No protection for your face or eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protection for your eyes but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes, but only a face shield can protect your entire face in a crash.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, what may you need to do?

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
Speed up before downshifting safely.
Swerve to the left.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting safely.
questions.explanation: Before shifting to a lower gear, slow down to a safe speed. Downshifting while going too fast can cause the motorcycle to lurch and the rear wheel to skid. When riding downhill or shifting into first gear, use the brakes to reach a safe speed before downshifting.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's space cushion should:

options.text: Always stay the same.
Change based on road and traffic conditions.
Not be necessary in most situations.
Be avoided to keep traffic moving safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or in heavy traffic when a driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: The front brake should be:

options.text: Too dangerous for new riders to use.
Used by itself.
Used occasionally to assist the rear brake.
Used with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Used with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Braking in a turn is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
Harder than braking on a straight road.
Done safely by using only the front brake.
Done safely by using only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes to brake in a turn, but you must know the right technique and be very careful.

questions.question: In a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider lean?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together at the same angle.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should stay upright.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should stay upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together at the same angle.
questions.explanation: In a normal turn, the motorcycle and rider should lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle should lean while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: To be seen in the rearview mirror of the driver ahead, you should ride:

options.text: In the center of the lane.
In the left side of the lane.
In the right side of the lane.
In a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Position yourself behind a car in the center of your lane. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?

options.text: The motorcycle's former owner.
The owner's manual.
A library book about motorcycles.
A motorcycle enthusiast.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: The owner's manual has information about your specific motorcycle. Read it before riding for the first time.

questions.question: When carrying a load in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Allow the load to move freely.
Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not move and affect how your motorcycle handles. Place the load toward the rear to prevent the sidecar from tipping during sharp left turns.

questions.question: How should you sit on your motorcycle for best control?

options.text: Sit with your arms propping you up rather than steering.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Allow your feet to hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you must stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to balance during turns. Use your arms to steer, not to support yourself. Sit close enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your feet on the footrests.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Accelerate out of the wobble.
Use the brakes immediately.
Grip the handlebars firmly and gradually close the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and gradually close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—it will make it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down gradually by closing the throttle. Shift your weight forward and downward. Pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not use the brakes, as they can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do with the brakes?

options.text: The rear brake should be applied first.
The front brake should be applied first.
Both brakes should be applied at the same time.
Only one brake, front or rear, should be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes should be applied at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Avoid other road users' blind spots.
Provide a good view of the shoulder.
Provide a poor view of road hazards.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid other road users' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and be seen by them. Do not stay in another driver's blind spot for long periods.

questions.question: When will a helmet NOT provide the best protection?

options.text: If it is certified by the DOT.
If it fits snugly.
If it is free of defects.
If it has cracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it has cracks.
questions.explanation: A helmet should meet DOT and state standards and fit snugly. It must be free of defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Is hearing protection needed when riding?

options.text: Not needed if you wear a helmet.
Needed in addition to a helmet.
Only needed on windy days.
Not needed if you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed in addition to a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Hearing protection guards against this while still letting you hear horns and sirens.

questions.question: When another vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Move onto the shoulder.
Allow the other driver to pass you.
Exit the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the other driver to pass you.
questions.explanation: Let the tailgater pass you. If safe, change lanes and let them go ahead. Speeding up may only increase danger by making them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular, white, and have black lettering or symbols. Speed limit signs tell you the rules you must follow on that road.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ is considered legally intoxicated.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In most places, a person age 21 or older is legally intoxicated at 0.08 percent BAC or higher. It is illegal and dangerous to drive any vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.
Ride under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hands near the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Begin slowing sooner than usual.
Begin slowing later than usual.
Apply the brakes more firmly than usual to stop quickly.
Apply the brakes more softly than usual to keep from overworking them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Begin slowing sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger in a sidecar affects how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will need more space to stop completely.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Gradually brake.
Accelerate.
Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—it makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by gradually closing the throttle. Shift your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.
